Class.name: IHC.ITF.FTP.Adapter.InboundAdapterSpecifyReadOrder
Class.Description: This is an extension of EnsLib.FTP.InboundAdapter that allows us to specify the read order the target files are read in

UDLText.name: T
UDLText.Content: /* override from File superclass with new description (FTP not File) */

Property.name: DeleteFromServer
Property.Description:
Specifies whether or not to delete files from the FTP server after successful processing
If not deleted, the adapter will ignore files already processed until something else removes them from the FTP server. NOTE: This has been modified from the original DeleteFromServer and is now set programatically, NOT by the user. To delete the source file, use the ActionOnSourceFile setting

Property.name: ActionOnSourceFile
Property.Description:
This is the action to be taken on the SOURCE file.

If the source file is to be left as is leave this field blank, but be aware this leaves the possibility the file will be processed again.

If you want to delete the source file from the server, enter DELETE (this replaces the original DeleteFromServer function).

If the source file needs to be renamed but remain in the current folder on the server, just enter the new name.

If the file needs to be moved to a new folder on the source server, include the full absolute path to the new location including the new file name.

NOTE: The following special values can also be included in the new file names:
%f - The original filename of the file
%CD - The date the file was processed in format 1970-01-01
%CT - The time the file was processed in format 12:00:00AM
%# - The current sequence number

EXAMPLE: Setting this value to %f_%CD_%CT_%# would rename testfile to something like

testfile_08/07/2015_02:39:23PM_1

Property.name: DirectoryContents

Property.name: %DirectoryContentsResultSet
Property.Description: ResultSet Used to get the contents of the current directory

Property.name: RegexFileFilter
Property.Description:
Regex pattern(s) to filter which files are processed. If multiple RegexFileFilters are specified (using the RegexFileFilterDelimiter), the files will be processed in the order they match the filters.

For example, if the RegexFileFilter is set to ^A.*;^B.* and the RegexFileFilterDelimiter is set to ; (semicolon) there will be two RegexFileFilters: ^A.* and ^B.* . This will cause all files that start with an A to process before all files that start with a B.

IMPORTANT: If you specify both a RegexFileFilter and a File Spec, only files that match the File Spec AND the RegexFileFilter(s) will be processed. To use only the Regex Filter, set File Spec to *. To use only the File Spec, leave the RegexFileFilter blank.

Property.name: RegexFileFilterDelimiter
Property.Description: The delimiter used to separate RegexFileFilters; if the character(s) specified in this field are present in the RegexFileFilter, the filter will be split into multiple filters. The can be used to allow multiple filters to be used, and also to allow files to be processed in a given order. See the RegexFileFilter for details.

Property.name: FileSpec
Property.Description:
Filename or wildcard file specification for file(s) to retrieve from the FTP server.

IMPORTANT: If you specify both a FileSpec and a RegexFileFilter, only files that match the File Spec AND the RegexFileFilter(s) will be processed. To use only the Regex Filter, set File Spec to *. To use only the File Spec, leave the RegexFileFilter blank.

Property.name: LoopThreshold
Property.Description: This is used to force the process to abandon after a given number of files processed (or attempted). In allows the component escape processing if endless processing loop occurs (for example: if processed files are renamed in a way that makes them get processed again). In general, this should be left at the default value of 25.
